title: Quiz: Effect of Catalysts on Rate

questions.stem: What is the definition of a catalyst?

options.text: A substance that increases the rate of a reaction without being used up
A substance that increases the yield of a reaction
A substance that is always consumed during a reaction
A substance that slows down a chemical reaction

questions.explanation: A catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without being chemically changed or used up in the process.

questions.stem: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?

options.text: By providing an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy
By increasing the surface area of the reactants
By increasing the concentration of the reactants
By increasing the temperature of the reactants

questions.explanation: A catalyst works by providing an alternative reaction pathway that has a lower activation energy. This means more particles have sufficient energy to react successfully.

options.text: Vitamins
Antibodies
Enzymes
Hormones

questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts found in living organisms. They speed up biochemical reactions and are highly specific, each enzyme catalysing only one particular reaction.

questions.stem: On an energy profile diagram, how does a catalyst affect the curve?

options.text: It changes the energy of the products
It raises the activation energy peak
It lowers the activation energy peak without changing the overall energy change
It increases the overall energy change of the reaction

questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy peak on the energy profile diagram, but the overall energy change (difference between reactants and products) remains the same.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a catalyst used in an industrial process?

options.text: Nitrogen in the Haber process
Carbon dioxide in the blast furnace
Water in the Contact process
Iron in the Haber process

questions.explanation: Iron is used as a catalyst in the Haber process, which manufactures ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen. It speeds up the reaction without being consumed.

questions.stem: Why are catalysts important in industrial chemistry?

options.text: They change the products of the reaction
They make reactions reversible
They reduce energy costs by allowing reactions to occur at lower temperatures
They increase the amount of product formed

questions.explanation: Catalysts allow reactions to proceed faster at lower temperatures, reducing the energy needed to heat reactants. This saves fuel costs and makes industrial processes more economical.

questions.stem: Which statement about catalysts is correct?

options.text: A catalyst can be used for any reaction
Catalysts are specific to particular reactions
Catalysts change the products of a reaction
A catalyst is always a metal

questions.explanation: Catalysts are specific: different reactions require different catalysts. A catalyst that works for one reaction may have no effect on another.
